title: Temporal Schedule identifiers, calendars and overlap values are not defined
source: Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
section: Batch and Scheduling Design v4, sheet Jobs, column When; Architecture v5 slide 44 (A4 job map) and slide 31 notes; Temporal and Drools design slide 12 (L3 kit, Scheduled job)
description: Ten live jobs become Temporal Schedules: JOB-06, JOB-10, JOB-14, JOB-16, JOB-17, JOB-18, JOB-19, JOB-20, JOB-21 and JOB-22. No source gives a Schedule ID, a cron expression, a Schedule-level overlap policy, a catch-up window or a time zone beyond the note that times are Asia/Bangkok. Times are stated as clock times or as cadence phrases: 'Daily 06:30', 'Daily 16:00', 'Nightly 02:00', 'Monthly, 3rd working day, on the ACE batch-complete record for ALS', 'Monthly, 1st Sunday', 'Every six months', 'Daily 00:01', 'Every 5 minutes', 'Daily 06:00'. Two of these cannot be written as a plain cron expression: JOB-16 must run on the third working day after AceDataReady, and JOB-17 runs on a weekday-dependent Sunday. The catalog and the design identify each Schedule by the job it serves and the name the source gives it, and carry the Schedule ID as the placeholder of Template and Rules R9.
evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4, sheet Jobs, rows JOB-06 to JOB-22, column When, holds the times above and no identifier. Architecture v5 slide 44 notes read 'a Temporal Schedule (cron, with overlap policy SKIP and catch-up window)' with no value per job. Temporal and Drools design slide 12 lists 'Scheduled job' as an L3 kit template with no parameters. Ownership Map v1, sheet Jobs, column Replacement, names the mechanism and the owner of each job and no identifier.
legacy_ref: JOB-06, JOB-10, JOB-14, JOB-16, JOB-17, JOB-18, JOB-19, JOB-20, JOB-21, JOB-22
proposed: Confirm one Schedule ID per job in the owning service, the cron or calendar expression with the Asia/Bangkok time zone, the overlap policy, the catch-up window and the pause-on-failure rule; decide whether JOB-16 is a cron Schedule with an AceDataReady gate inside the workflow or an event-started run on the third working day.

title: Activity timeouts, heartbeat intervals and task-queue limits are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
section: Architecture v5 slide 11 (contract, timeout and retry table); Temporal and Drools design slides 14, 27 and 28
description: The design fixes the activity retry policy (1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts) and the non-retryable NoPackageInForce failure, but no source gives a start-to-close timeout, a schedule-to-close timeout, a heartbeat interval or a task-queue rate limit for any activity. Architecture v5 slide 11 states only 'start-to-close per activity; backoff; heartbeats'. The rule evaluation target is under 300 ms and the agent run is capped at 60 s, and neither is written as an activity timeout. A worker that hangs therefore blocks its task until the workflow's default timeout, which is not stated either.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11, row Timeout, retry, column for the activity contract, reads 'Start-to-close per activity; backoff; heartbeats'. Temporal and Drools design slide 14 gives 'Retry policy: 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts; NoPackageInForce is non-retryable' and names no timeout. Slide 28 repeats the retry policy. Slide 32 item 6 lists Temporal 1.30+ and jobs as Schedules as the platform open points and says nothing about timeouts.
proposed: Set a start-to-close timeout and a heartbeat interval per activity contract (EvaluateRules, RecordAndApply, the payment, document, partner, integration and reporting activities) and a task-queue rate limit per service, and publish them in the contract jar of each service.

title: The event-started payment workflow of JOB-07 and JOB-08 has no name
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
section: Architecture v5 slide 44 (A4 job map) rows JOB-07 and JOB-08, slide 17 (rwb-payment contracts); Temporal and Drools design slide 14 note
description: Architecture v5 slide 44 makes JOB-07 payment matching and JOB-08 booking confirmation event-started workflows in rwb-payment, and the Temporal and Drools design names the activities matchPayments and confirmBookings that they run. No source names the workflow that hosts those activities, gives it a workflow ID or says whether one workflow hosts both jobs or each job has its own. The catalog lists both rows with the workflow name as the R9 placeholder and the activity as the only known step.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 rows JOB-07 and JOB-08 give the mechanism 'event-triggered workflow' with owner rwb-payment and no name. Slide 17 names 'Act: matchPayments, confirmBookings'. Temporal and Drools design slide 14 note reads 'rwb-payment's matchPayments activity (JOB-07, started by AceDataReady)', which names the activity and not the workflow.
proposed: Name the workflow, its ID scheme (one run per business date and payment run key), and whether matchPayments and confirmBookings run in one workflow or two.

title: The work started by six Schedules and three workflows is not named
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
section: Architecture v5 slides 14, 15, 16 and 44; Batch and Scheduling Design v4, sheet Jobs; Temporal and Drools design slides 12 and 23
description: Six of the ten target Schedules name neither the workflow nor the activity they start: rebalancing (JOB-06) is only 'Act: allocate, transfer, rebalance' on rwb-case; retention (JOB-17) only 'Schedule: retention' on rwb-document; access review list (JOB-18) only 'Schedule: access review list (six-monthly)' on rwb-access; re-appraisal (JOB-19) only 'Schedule: re-appraisal monthly' on rwb-asset; chain check (JOB-14) only 'Schedule: chain check 02:00' on rwb-decision; rule promote (JOB-20) is described in the v4 row text and publishes RulePackageInForce with no activity named. The two P1 workflows AceIngestCheck and reconciliation have no activity names either, the OCR, classify and extract steps of DocumentIntakeWorkflow are named as steps and not as activities, and the platform smoke workflow of JOB-22 is named with no statement of what it calls.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 TMP cells read 'Schedules: rule promote 00:01, chain check 02:00' and 'Act: allocate, transfer, rebalance'; slide 16 reads 'DocumentIntakeWorkflow: OCR, classify, extract; Act: generate, seal - Schedule: retention'; slide 44 gives the mechanism only. Batch and Scheduling Design v4 rows JOB-06 and JOB-14 to JOB-20 describe the work and no workflow. Temporal and Drools design slide 12 names the kit template 'Scheduled job' and no per-job content.
legacy_ref: JOB-06, JOB-14, JOB-17, JOB-18, JOB-19, JOB-20
proposed: Name the activity or workflow each Schedule starts, its input (business date or run key), its output and whether it is idempotent for a re-run of the same business date.

title: DailyCaseRun is described both as a Schedule and as an event-started workflow
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Architecture v5 slide 14 (contract of rwb-case, TMP cell) and slide 44 (A4 job map) row JOB-02
description: Architecture v5 slide 14 writes 'DailyCaseRun (Schedule + AceDataReady)' and slide 44 writes 'AceDataReady -> DailyCaseRun' for the same job. The two readings differ for build: a Schedule needs a cron, an overlap policy and a catch-up window, and an event-started workflow needs an event contract and an idempotency key. The design lists the job as event-started and records the Schedule as a fallback that is not configured in the target.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 TMP cell: 'CaseWorkflow (parent, one per case) - DailyCaseRun (Schedule + AceDataReady) - Act: allocate, transfer, rebalance'. Slide 44 row JOB-02: 'Airflow: ACE data ready | rwb-case | AceDataReady -> DailyCaseRun'. Slide 31 notes make AceDataReady the trigger of the morning run.
proposed: Confirm that DailyCaseRun is started by AceDataReady only in the target, and that the Schedule named on slide 14 is a fallback for a day when Airflow does not signal the business date.

title: The rwb-platform task queue has no service definition
source: Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Batch and Scheduling Design v4, sheet Jobs, row JOB-22 column What it does and row JOB-21; Architecture v5 slide 44 rows JOB-21 and JOB-22; Ownership Map v1, sheet Services
description: JOB-21 the stuck workflow scan and JOB-22 the platform smoke run on task queue rwb-platform. rwb-platform is not one of the 19 service queues of the Ownership Map Services sheet, and no source says which deployment hosts the platform worker, whether that worker has a schema of its own in the ACE database, what its queue name is in a lower environment, or how its task queue is rate-limited. The ownership of both jobs is given as platform (PLT) with no service code.
evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-22 reads 'Starts PlatformSmokeWorkflow as platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} on task queue rwb-platform through WorkflowGateway'. Architecture v5 slide 44 gives owner 'platform' for JOB-21 and JOB-22. Ownership Map v1 sheet Services lists 19 rows, P1 to P10 and S1 to S9, and none is rwb-platform.
proposed: Define the platform worker: the deployment that hosts it, the task queue name per environment, its schema or its lack of one, and the quotas of the rwb-platform queue.

title: The case workflow ID is written two ways
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v3
section: Temporal and Drools design slide 13 note; ADR-011
description: Temporal and Drools design slide 13 says the CaseWorkflow workflow ID is the case ID and adds that ADR-011 writes it as case-{caseId}. The two forms behave differently: signalWithStart creates a second run if the ID does not match, and the JOB-21 visibility query filters on workflow IDs and search attributes. The catalog does not choose one in the workflow row and records the case ID of the v5 design, with this row as the decision point.
evidence: Temporal and Drools design slide 13 note: 'CaseWorkflow (workflow ID = case ID; ADR-011 writes it as case-{caseId})'. Slide 30 note: 'the CaseWorkflow (ID = case ID) starts on queue rwb-case'. ADR-011 is named as the source of the other form.
proposed: Confirm one workflow ID form for CaseWorkflow and apply it to the case router's signalWithStart, to the child workflow IDs of the stage workflows and to the JOB-21 visibility query.
